questions.question: An article is sold for ₹ x after offering two successive discounts of 25% and 8% on its marked price of ₹500. The value of x is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Effective Discount % = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂ / 100)

Effective Discount = 25 + 8 − (25 × 8 / 100) = 33 − 2 = 31%

Selling Price (x) = (100% − 31%) of **Marked Price**

x = 69% of 500 = 0.69 × 500 = 345

**∴ The correct answer is ₹345.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price** (MP) = ₹500

First discount (d₁) = 25%

Second discount (d₂) = 8%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bdfe112533a268be9d08db3678757b05f8aaa0d32d26e82cdf7500992f45bcd4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after first 25% discount = 500 × (1 − 25/100)

⇒ Price after first discount = 500 × (75/100) = ₹375

⇒ Price after second 8% discount (x) = 375 × (1 − 8/100)

⇒ x = 375 × (92/100)

⇒ x = 375 × 0.92

⇒ x = 345

**∴ The correct answer is ₹345.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price and Selling Price

The **Marked Price** is the price printed on the label, and **Selling Price** is the final amount paid after all discounts: SP = MP × (100 − d%)/100.

Net Discount Value

The total discount in rupees is the difference between the **Marked Price** and the **Selling Price**: Discount = MP − SP.

questions.question: Which organelle is found ONLY in plant cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

**Note: **The correct answer as per the official answer key is **Mitochondria** but in actual the correct answer would be **chloroplast** as they are only found in plant cells which allows plants to produce their own food using sunlight.

__
 
• Chloroplasts are found only in plant cells and certain algae, and they are not present in animal cells.
 
• They are responsible for photosynthesis, a process that converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
 
• Chloroplasts contain the pigment chlorophyll, which captures light energy.
 
• These organelles have their own DNA and replicate independently of the cell.
 
• Chloroplasts have a double membrane structure with an inner network of thylakoid membranes where the light reactions of photosynthesis occur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• Known as the powerhouses of the cell, they generate most of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration.
 
• Present in both plant and animal cells.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**
 
 
• These are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes responsible for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• Lysosomes are generally found in animal cells. They are found in plant cells in some rare conditions.
 
• They are often referred to as the "digestive system" of the cell because they help in the degradation of macromolecules.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**
 
 
• It is a network of membranes within the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells, involved in protein and lipid synthesis.
 
• The ER is divided into two types: rough ER (with ribosomes) and smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and folding, while smooth ER is associated with lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.

**Total Time** = 10 hr

Average Speed

It is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Unit Conversion

Relative Speed

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

Statements:

I) A current carrying conductor acts like a magnet.

II) Moving electrons perpendicular to the magnetic field do not experience any force.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statement I only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A current-carrying conductor generates a magnetic field around it, behaving like a magnet (Statement I is correct).
 
• Moving electrons perpendicular to the magnetic field experience a force called the Lorentz force (Statement II is incorrect).
 
• The direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor can be determined using the right-hand thumb rule.
 
• The magnitude of the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying conductor is directly proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the distance from the conductor.
 
• Electromagnets are practical applications of the principle that a current-carrying conductor acts like a magnet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge**

 
 
• The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by the equation F = q(v × B), where q is the charge, v is the velocity, and B is the magnetic field.
 
• The direction of the force is perpendicular to both the velocity of the charge and the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**
 
 
• Electromagnetic induction is the process by which a changing magnetic field induces an electric current in a conductor.
 
• This phenomenon is the principle behind the operation of transformers, electric generators, and inductors.

questions.question: Three years ago, the average age of a family of six members was 19 years. Since then a boy has been born and the average age of the family is the same today as it was three years ago. What is the age of the boy?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **average age** remains the **same** after **n years** and adding **one new member**:

Age of new member = **Average − (Initial Members × Years Passed)**

Age of the boy = 19 − (6 × 3)

⇒ Age = 19 − 18 = 1 year.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 year.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **family members** = 6

**Average age** 3 years ago = 19 years

Current **average age** (including boy) = 19 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3be8daf0027a7f8c2ae818897121d772f63994795cc57b177367cc9f341e3d6a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total age** of 6 members 3 years ago = 6 × 19 = 114 years

⇒ **Total age** of these 6 members **today** = 114 + (6 × 3) = 114 + 18 = 132 years

⇒ Total family members **today** = 6 + 1 (boy) = 7 members

⇒ **Total age** of 7 members today = 7 × 19 = 133 years

⇒ **Age of the boy** = Total age of 7 members − Total age of 6 members

⇒ Age of the boy = 133 − 132 = 1 year

**∴ The correct answer is 1 year.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Age Concept

The **average** of a group is the sum of all values divided by the total count (Average = Sum ÷ Count).

Age Shift Rule

If every person in a group grows older by **'n' years**, the average age of the group also increases by exactly **'n' years**.

New Member Addition

Value of **new member** = (New Average × New Count) − (Old Average × Old Count).</p

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about Rutherford’s model of an atom?

options.text: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths.
There is a positively charged centre in an atom, which is called the nucleus.
Electrons revolve around the nucleus in elliptical paths.

questions.solution:
The incorrect answer is __**Electrons revolve around the nucleus in elliptical paths.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rutherford’s model of an atom proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus in **circular paths** called orbits.
 
• The nucleus is a small, dense, positively charged center within the atom.
 
• The size of the nucleus is very small compared to the size of the atom.
 
• Rutherford's model could not explain the stability of the atom as it did not account for energy loss by electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Limitations of Rutherford’s Model**

• Did not account for atomic spectra.

questions.question: If a sum of money doubles itself in 10 years on compound interest, then in how many years will it become 16 times of itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n** times in **T** years, it becomes **nk** times in **T × k** years.

Given: Sum becomes **2 times** in **10 years** (n = 2, T = 10).

Target: Sum becomes **16 times**.

⇒ 16 = 2⁴ (So, **k = 4**).

⇒ Required time = T × k = 10 × 4 = **40 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Sum = **P**

Time (n₁) = **10 years**

Amount (A₁) = **2P**

Target Amount (A₂) = **16P**

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a57fd7e06ffbadaab8a9f3b2eab8a4879fb5cc45cd04ad8b07a6911d49a24fd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁰

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁰ ... (Equation 1)

For the sum to become 16 times (16P) in **T** years:

⇒ 16P = P(1 + r/100)T

⇒ 16 = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ 2⁴ = (1 + r/100)T

Substitute the value of 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ ((1 + r/100)¹⁰)⁴ = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁴⁰ = (1 + r/100)T

Comparing powers on both sides:

⇒ T = 40 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A is calculated as A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt, where n is the number of times interest is compounded per unit t.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate doubling time is by dividing 72 by the annual **interest rate** (t ≈ 72/r).

SI vs CI for First Year

For the first year (or first compounding period), the **Simple Interest** and **Compound Interest** on the same principal and rate are always equal.

Successive Growth

Compound interest follows a **Geometric Progression (GP)** where the common ratio is (1 + r/100).</p

questions.question: Two angles are complementary. The larger angle is 6° less than five times the measure of the smaller angle. What is the measure of the larger angle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of **complementary angles** = 90°.

Let the **smaller angle** be 1 unit.

Then the **larger angle** = 5 units − 6°.

Sum: 1 unit + 5 units − 6° = 90° ⇒ 6 units = 96°.

⇒ 1 unit = 16° (smaller angle).

**Larger angle** = 90° − 16° = 74°.

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ The two angles are **complementary** (sum = 90°).

⇒ The **larger angle** is 6° less than 5 times the **smaller angle**.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Sum of complementary angles: α + β = 90°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa26acdf097a7c6ea6336856c5df6eb68ec0fe2d0e1c65eafd825a0e150ecaf5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the measure of the **smaller angle** be x.

⇒ According to the question, the **larger angle** = 5x − 6.

⇒ x + (5x − 6) = 90

⇒ 6x − 6 = 90

⇒ 6x = 90 + 6

⇒ 6x = 96

⇒ x = 96 ÷ 6 = 16°

⇒ **Larger angle** = 5(16) − 6 = 80 − 6 = 74°.

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are said to be supplementary if the sum of their measures is exactly 180°.

Linear Pair of Angles

A pair of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines, where the sum of the angles is always 180°.

Adjacent Angles

Angles that share a common vertex and a common side but do not overlap.</p

questions.question: The relation between focal length ‘f’, object distance ‘u’ and image distance ‘v’ in the case of reflection of light by a spherical mirror is given by ________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The formula 1/f = (1/u) + (1/v) is known as the **mirror equation** or the **mirror formula**.
 
• This equation applies to both concave and convex mirrors, with the appropriate sign conventions.
 
• In the equation, **f** represents the focal length of the mirror, **u** is the object distance from the mirror, and **v** is the image distance from the mirror.
 
• The mirror equation is derived from the geometry of the mirror and the laws of reflection.
 
• This relationship helps in determining the position and nature (real or virtual) of the image formed by spherical mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Concave Mirrors**
 
 
• These mirrors can produce real and inverted images or virtual and erect images depending on the position of the object.
 
• They are used in applications like shaving mirrors, reflecting telescopes, and headlights of vehicles.

questions.question: Amita is 2 years older than her friend Amrita. Amita's father is twice as old as Amita, and Amrita is twice as old as her sister. The ages of Amita's father and Amrita's sister differ by 43 years. The sum of the ages (in years) of Amita and Amrita is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Amrita's sister's** age be x years.

**Amrita** = 2x, **Amita** = 2x + 2, **Father** = 2(2x + 2) = 4x + 4.

Given: Father − Sister = 43 ⇒ (4x + 4) − x = 43 ⇒ 3x = 39 ⇒ x = 13.

Sum of **Amita** and **Amrita** = (2x + 2) + 2x = 4x + 2 = 4(13) + 2 = 54 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 54 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amita** = **Amrita** + 2

**Father** = 2 × **Amita**

**Amrita** = 2 × **Sister**

**Father** − **Sister** = 43 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da610ec88fdb23c188a7ef1a99556bc879753de60f293320b992569721a36515.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let **Amrita's** age be M years.

⇒ **Amita's** age (A) = M + 2

⇒ **Father's** age (F) = 2(M + 2) = 2M + 4

⇒ **Sister's** age (S) = M ÷ 2

⇒ F − S = 43

⇒ (2M + 4) − (M ÷ 2) = 43

⇒ 2M − 0.5M = 43 − 4

⇒ 1.5M = 39

⇒ M = 39 ÷ 1.5 = 26 years

⇒ **Amita's** age (A) = 26 + 2 = 28 years

⇒ Sum = A + M = 28 + 26 = 54 years

**∴ The correct answer is 54 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two persons always remains **constant** regardless of the number of years passed or preceding.

Linear Equation Formulation

In age problems, it is always efficient to assume the age of the **youngest person** or the **reference person** as 'x' to simplify calculations.

Ratio in Ages

If the ratio of ages is given for different time periods, use the concept of **ratio balancing** by making the age difference units equal across the time gaps.</p

questions.question:
Simplify the following expression:

(a + 2b - c)(b - c) + (a - c)2b + b²
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **substitution method** by assuming values for the variables: Let **a = 1, b = 1, and c = 1**.

Expression: (1 + 2 − 1)(1 − 1) + (1 − 1) × 2 × 1 + 1² = 2 × 0 + 0 + 1 = **1**.

Check the options for value 1: 3(1)² + 1² + 3(1)(1) − 5(1)(1) − (1)(1) = 3 + 1 + 3 − 5 − 1 = **1**.

**∴ The correct answer is 3b²+c²+3ab-5bc-ac.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (a + 2b − c)(b − c) + (a − c)2b + b²

**Formula Used:** **Distributive Property** of multiplication over addition/subtraction: x(y + z) = xy + xz.

⇒ Expand the first term (a + 2b − c)(b − c):

⇒ a(b − c) + 2b(b − c) − c(b − c) = ab − ac + 2b² − 2bc − bc + c²

⇒ 2b² + c² + ab − 3bc − ac

⇒ Expand the second term (a − c)2b:

⇒ 2ab − 2bc

⇒ Now, combine all parts of the expression:

⇒ (2b² + c² + ab − 3bc − ac) + (2ab − 2bc) + b²

⇒ Group the **like terms** together: (2b² + b²) + c² + (ab + 2ab) + (−3bc − 2bc) − ac

⇒ 3b² + c² + 3ab − 5bc − ac

**∴ The correct answer is 3b²+c²+3ab-5bc-ac.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Expansion

Multiplying two polynomials involves multiplying each term of the first polynomial by every term of the second and then simplifying the result.

Like Terms

Terms that have the same variables raised to the same powers are called **like terms**; they can be added or subtracted from each other.

BODMAS Rule

Always perform operations inside **brackets** first, followed by multiplication, and finally addition/subtraction to avoid errors during simplification.</p

questions.question: A trader lost 20% by selling a watch for ₹1,024. What percentage will he gain by selling it for ₹1,472?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Selling at a **20% loss** means the **Selling Price** is **80%** of the **Cost Price**.

Applying the **Unitary Method**: ₹1,024 → 80%

Therefore, ₹1,472 → (80 ÷ 1024) × 1472 = 115%

Since the new percentage is **115%**, the gain is 115% − 100% = **15%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** = ₹1,024

Initial **Loss Percentage** = 20%

New **Selling Price (SP₂)** = ₹1,472

**Formula Used:**

**Cost Price (CP)** = [SP × 100] / [100 − Loss%]

**Gain Percentage** = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c49122c9cf366f54898e999d079441cfc224c0210830d03909d2f755dc459ab.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (1024 × 100) / (100 − 20)

⇒ CP = (1024 × 100) / 80

⇒ CP = 12.8 × 100 = ₹1,280

⇒ New Profit = SP₂ − CP = 1472 − 1280 = ₹192

⇒ Gain Percentage = (192 / 1280) × 100

⇒ Gain Percentage = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Base

Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless specifically mentioned otherwise in the question.

Selling Price Formula

The direct relationship is SP = CP × (100 ± Percentage Change) / 100, where ± represents **Profit (+)** or **Loss (−)**.

Marked Price and Discount

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a small tree from a point on the ground 300 m away from the foot of the tree was 30°. When the tree grew taller, its angle of elevation became 60° from the same point. By how much did the tree grow?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Growth in height = Distance × (tan θ₂ − tan θ₁)

Here, Distance = 300 m, θ₁ = 30°, and θ₂ = 60°

Growth = 300 × (tan 60° − tan 30°) = 300 × (√3 − 1/√3)

Growth = 300 × (2/√3) = 600/√3 = 200√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 200√3 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance from foot (AB) = 300 m

Initial **angle of elevation** (θ₁) = 30°

Final **angle of elevation** (θ₂) = 60°

**Formula used:**

tan θ = **Height** / **Base**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/025aea6a7dc433aae2e9b2c16dd63759948ce7c8eede663f238802fc193c4c4b.png] 

In triangle ABPᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ:

⇒ tan 30° = h₁ / 300

⇒ 1 / √3 = h₁ / 300

⇒ h₁ = 300 / √3 = 100√3 m

In triangle ABPfᵢₙₐₗ:

⇒ tan 60° = h₂ / 300

⇒ √3 = h₂ / 300

⇒ h₂ = 300√3 m

**Growth of the tree** = h₂ − h₁

⇒ Growth = 300√3 − 100√3

⇒ Growth = 200√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 200√3 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

It is the angle between the horizontal line of sight and the line joining the observer's eye to the **object above** the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios

For a constant distance, **height** is directly proportional to the **tangent** of the angle: h = d × tan θ.

Standard Tangent Values

tan 30° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3 ≈ 1.732.

Height Difference Property

If the base is d and the angle changes from θ₁ to θ₂, the **vertical change** is Δh = d(tan θ₂ − tan θ₁).</p

questions.question: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 7 : 10. Find the difference between the greatest and the smallest angles of the quadrilateral.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **ratio parts** = 2 + 5 + 7 + 10 = 24 units.

Total **internal angles** of a quadrilateral = 360°.

⇒ 24 units = 360° ⇒ 1 unit = 15°.

**Difference** between greatest (10) and smallest (2) parts = 10 − 2 = 8 units.

⇒ Difference = 8 × 15° = 120°.

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of angles = 2 : 5 : 7 : 10.

**Formula Used:** Sum of all interior angles of a **quadrilateral** is always 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61b2a819f1131ba03ae6cc2fbb990d82a34444d7a779435098af6853e38d7178.png] 

⇒ Let the four angles be 2x, 5x, 7x, and 10x respectively.

⇒ 2x + 5x + 7x + 10x = 360°

⇒ 24x = 360°

⇒ x = 360° ÷ 24

⇒ x = 15°

⇒ **Smallest angle** = 2x = 2 × 15° = 30°

⇒ **Greatest angle** = 10x = 10 × 15° = 150°

⇒ **Difference** = 150° − 30° = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property of Polygons

The sum of internal angles of any polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of **opposite angles** is always 180°.

Exterior Angle Sum

The sum of all **exterior angles** of any convex quadrilateral (or any polygon) is always 360°.</p

Use the **Successive Percentage Change** formula: Net Change = x + y + (xy ÷ 100)

Here, x = −10% (tax reduction) and y = +20% (consumption increase).

Net change in **Tax Revenue** = −10 + 20 + [(−10 × 20) ÷ 100]

⇒ Net change = 10 − 2 = 8%

Since the result is positive, it indicates an **increase**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Increase in Revenue = 10,800 − 10,000 = ₹800

⇒ Percentage Increase = (800 ÷ 10,000) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

Revenue-Consumption Relation

Successive Percentage for Geometry

questions.question: If (584)² = 3,41,056, then the value of square root of 34.1056 is:

Given that 584² = 341056, it follows that √341056 = 584.

The number 34.1056 has **4 decimal places**.

When taking a **square root**, the number of decimal places is **halved** (4 ÷ 2 = 2).

Therefore, we shift the decimal in 584 two places to the left to get 5.84.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.84.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Square of 584 = 3,41,056

Value to find = √34.1056

**Formula Used:**

√(x ÷ y) = √x ÷ √y

⇒ √34.1056 = √(341056 ÷ 10000)

⇒ √341056 ÷ √10000

⇒ 584 ÷ 100

⇒ 5.84

**∴ The correct answer is 5.84.**

**__Additional Information__**

Decimal Rule in Square Roots

If a perfect square has 2n digits after the decimal point, its square root will have exactly n digits after the decimal point.

Square Root of Powers of 10

The square root of 10²ⁿ is always 10ⁿ. For example, √10000 = √10⁴ = 10² = 100.

questions.question: The radius of a cylinder is 5 cm more than its height. If the curved surface area of the cylinder is 792 cm², then the volume of the cylinder (in cm³), is ________. [Use pi = (22)/(7) ]

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h = 792 ⇒ π × r × h = 396

Volume of a cylinder is π × r² × h = (π × r × h) × r = 396 × r

Since 2 × (22/7) × r × (r − 5) = 792 ⇒ r × (r − 5) = 126

By simple observation, 14 × (14 − 5) = 126, so the radius r = 14 cm

Volume = 396 × 14 = 5544 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 5544 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of cylinder (r) = height (h) + 5

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 792 cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90e5452c5c92732388895bd613d39b0b616a48b1d86763138ca5097202c8bd9a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × (h + 5) × h = 792

⇒ (44/7) × (h² + 5h) = 792

⇒ h² + 5h = 792 × 7 ÷ 44

⇒ h² + 5h = 18 × 7

⇒ h² + 5h − 126 = 0

⇒ h² + 14h − 9h − 126 = 0

⇒ h(h + 14) − 9(h + 14) = 0

⇒ (h − 9)(h + 14) = 0

⇒ h = 9 cm (since height cannot be negative)

⇒ Radius (r) = 9 + 5 = 14 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (14)² × 9

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 196 × 9 = 22 × 28 × 9

⇒ Volume = 616 × 9 = 5544 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 5544 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Cylinder

A cylinder is a 3D solid with two parallel circular bases. Total Surface Area (TSA) = CSA + 2 × Base Area = 2 × π × r × (r + h).

Volume of Related Shapes

The volume of a cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder is exactly one-third of the cylinder's volume. Cone Volume = (1/3) × π × r² × h.

Circumference and Area of Base

The base of a cylinder is a circle. Base Area = π × r² and Base Perimeter (Circumference) = 2 × π × r. The CSA can directly be calculated as Base Perimeter × height.

questions.question: The highest common factor of a set of coprime numbers is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Coprime numbers** (or relatively prime numbers) are defined as numbers that share no common factors other than **1**.

Since the only common factor is 1, the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** must be 1.

Example: For the set {8, 9}, the factors of 8 are {1, 2, 4, 8} and the factors of 9 are {1, 3, 9}. The only common factor is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A set of **coprime numbers**.

**Definition:** Two or more numbers are **coprime** if their **greatest common divisor** is exactly 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/beb015cf070bd7d2d2dfc7988b7c1656b8aa9485cd88c08466ede00d6822b0be.png] 

⇒ Let the set of numbers be {x, y}.

⇒ Factors of x = {1, f₁, f₂, ...}

⇒ Factors of y = {1, g₁, g₂, ...}

⇒ If x and y are coprime, then {1, f₁, f₂, ...} ∩ {1, g₁, g₂, ...} = {1}.

⇒ The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is the largest value in the intersection set.

⇒ HCF = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM of Coprime Numbers

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of a set of coprime numbers is always equal to their **product** (e.g., LCM of 5 and 7 is 35).

Consecutive Numbers

Any two **consecutive natural numbers** (like 14 and 15) are always **coprime** to each other.

HCF and LCM Relationship

For any two numbers a and b, **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**. For coprime numbers, this simplifies to 1 × LCM = a × b.

Prime Numbers

Two different **prime numbers** are always coprime, but coprime numbers themselves do not necessarily have to be prime (e.g., 8 and 9 are coprime but composite).</p

questions.question: From a 2.25-litre mango drink bottle, how many small glasses of 45 ml can be filled?

Decimal Multiplication

questions.question: Ravi and Kumar are working on an assignment. Ravi takes 6 hours to type 32 pages on a computer, while Kumar takes 5 hours to type 40 pages. How much time will they take, working together on two different computers to type an assignment of 110 pages?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Ravi's** rate = 32 ÷ 6 = 16/3 pages/hr.

**Kumar's** rate = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 pages/hr.

**Combined rate** = 16/3 + 8 = 40/3 pages/hr.

Time for **110 pages** = 110 ÷ (40/3) = 33/4 = 8.25 hours = 8 hr 15 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hr 15 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ravi** types 32 pages in 6 hours.

**Kumar** types 40 pages in 5 hours.

Total assignment size = 110 pages.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Rate × Time ⇒ Rate = Work ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d71d3522f70483627ce209df9e4df1cbefe6583172558576e77d26db960503b1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Typing speed of **Ravi** = 32/6 = 16/3 pages/hr

⇒ Typing speed of **Kumar** = 40/5 = 8 pages/hr

⇒ Combined speed = (16/3 + 8) pages/hr

⇒ Combined speed = (16 + 24) ÷ 3 = 40/3 pages/hr

⇒ Time taken to type **110 pages** = 110 ÷ (40/3)

⇒ Time = (110 × 3) ÷ 40 = 330 ÷ 40 = 33/4 hours

⇒ Time = 8.25 hours

⇒ 8.25 hours = 8 hours + (0.25 × 60) minutes

⇒ Time = 8 hours 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hr 15 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work-Rate Relationship

The total work done is calculated as the product of the **efficiency** (rate) and the **time** taken: Work = Rate × Time.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple entities work simultaneously, their **individual rates** are additive: Rₜₒₜₐₗ = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rₙ.

Time Conversion

To convert a fractional hour into minutes, **multiply the decimal portion** by 60. For example, 0.25 hours = 0.25 × 60 = 15 minutes.</p

questions.question: When 10% of the inhabitants of a village died of cholera, a panic set in, during which 25% of the remaining inhabitants left the village. The population then reduced to 4050. Find the number of original inhabitants.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **fractional multiplier method**: 10% death means 9/10 remains; 25% leaving means 3/4 remains.

Let the **original inhabitants** be **x**.

x × (9/10) × (3/4) = 4050

x × (27/40) = 4050 ⇒ x = 150 × 40 = 6000

**∴ The correct answer is 6000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Death rate from **cholera** = 10%

Inhabitants who left during **panic** = 25% of the remaining

**Final population** = 4050

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32d1a904d3919ad8d5b002472953b580e85c324b9a5865d4e62d0666df535468.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **original population** be P.

⇒ Population after cholera = P − (10% of P) = 0.90P

⇒ Population after panic = 0.90P − (25% of 0.90P)

⇒ Population after panic = 0.90P × (1 − 0.25) = 0.90P × 0.75

⇒ 4050 = P × 0.90 × 0.75

⇒ 4050 = P × 0.675

⇒ P = 4050 ÷ 0.675

⇒ P = 4050000 ÷ 675 = 6000

**∴ The correct answer is 6000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Decrease

If a value is decreased by a% and then by b%, the effective remaining value is Initial × (1 − a/100) × (1 − b/100).

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

10% = 1/10 (Remaining = 9/10) and 25% = 1/4 (Remaining = 3/4). Multiplying these fractions helps in solving **population change** problems faster.

Net Percentage Change Formula

For two successive changes x% and y%, the net change is [x + y + (xy/100)]%. For decreases, use negative values.</p

questions.question: The sum of the length, the breadth and the height of a cuboid is 38 cm and the length of its diagonal is 22 cm. Find the total surface area of the cuboid.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct algebraic identity: (l + b + h)² = (l² + b² + h²) + 2(lb + bh + hl)

Here, (l² + b² + h²) = Diagonal² and 2(lb + bh + hl) = **Total Surface Area** (TSA).

Shortcut formula: **TSA** = (Sum of dimensions)² − (Diagonal)²

⇒ **TSA** = 38² − 22² = 1444 − 484 = 960 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 960 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of **length**, **breadth**, and **height** (l + b + h) = 38 cm

Length of the **diagonal** (d) = 22 cm

**Formula Used:**

1. **Diagonal of a cuboid** = √(l² + b² + h²)

2. **Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 2(lb + bh + hl)

3. Algebraic identity: (l + b + h)² = l² + b² + h² + 2(lb + bh + hl)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/301db4b1b6ed1db5d9f4f295cf5a8fbf56cdd5c1197c5ea5afdc2a0fc2875790.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²) = 22

⇒ Squaring both sides: l² + b² + h² = 22² = 484

⇒ We know (l + b + h) = 38

⇒ Squaring both sides: (l + b + h)² = 38²

⇒ l² + b² + h² + 2(lb + bh + hl) = 1444

⇒ 484 + **TSA** = 1444

⇒ **TSA** = 1444 − 484

⇒ **TSA** = 960 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 960 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The space occupied by a cuboid is given by the product of its three dimensions: **Volume** = l × b × h.

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the four side walls of the cuboid (excluding top and bottom) is **LSA** = 2h(l + b).

Special Case: Cube

When l = b = h = a, the cuboid becomes a cube. **Diagonal** = a√3, **TSA** = 6a², and **Volume** = a³.</p

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c446a2bbddaca49ebabea5f3c0e63c81171b36cdd700655305cdd7b4ec4cd59.png]

Mean Proportional

Third Proportional

In the continued proportion a:b = b:c, the term 'c' is called the **third proportional** to a and b, calculated as c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If four quantities a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a:b = c:d), then d is the **fourth proportional**, where d = (b × c) ÷ a.</p
